previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of two kidney transplants was readmitted the day after discharge due to sudden swelling and pain in her right arm, where a midline catheter had been placed for outpatient antibiotic treatment of E. coli bacteremia and pyelonephritis. Imaging revealed a deep vein thrombosis around the catheter in the basilic vein. The midline was removed, and she was started on intravenous heparin, later transitioned to oral apixaban. She received two additional doses of intravenous ceftriaxone and was discharged on a short course of oral cefpodoxime to complete her antibiotic treatment. During admission, she experienced mild diarrhea, which resolved without evidence of C. difficile. Her glucose levels remained elevated, and she was advised to follow up with her diabetes team. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for ongoing care across multiple specialties.
problems: Right upper extremity deep vein thrombosis
Pyelonephritis as a complication of transplant
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy

UTI with UCx from ___ growing Klebsiella, initially meeting

immunocompromised state, h/o renal transplant and diabetes, she 
was started on broad spectrum coverage with 1 dose of cefepime 
in the ED and switched to ceftazidime on the floor. UCx from 
___ was confirmed to be growing Klebsiella (sensitivities

ciprofloxacin for a 14-day course. There were no signs of 
tenderness over her graft throughout her hospital course.
